newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, Taiwan activists end isles protest, sail home.
newsitem.headline: HK, Taiwan activists end isles protest, sail home.

text.p: Hong Kong and Taiwan organisers of a challenge to Tokyo's claim to an East China Sea archipelago ended their high-seas protest on Monday after facing an impenetrable force of Japanese coast guards.

Activists initially acceded to a Taiwan request that they withdraw to 20 nautical miles or more from the disputed islands and by mid-afternoon said they had decided to end the protest. The 20-boat protest flotilla was returning to Taiwan.

In a show of force that contrasted sharply with Tokyo's meek response to a similar 1996 protests, Japan deployed 60 coast guard vessels -- some armed -- and used their superior numbers to keep the 20-odd Taiwan and Hong Kong boats at bay.

Two activists leapt from the 100-tonne Protect-the-Diaoyus, a Hong Kong pleasure boat leading Monday's protest voyage, onto a Japanese patrol boat but were being put back aboard without arrest, Japan's Maritime Safety Agency said.
In September, a Hong Kong activist who jumped into stormy waters during an abortive islands voyage drowned.
Taiwan's navy, air force and coast guard were ready to mount emergency rescues if necessary, but were adopting a principle of non-involvement, the defence ministry said.
